snippet.title: Missing people in Mexico – in the shadow of the World Cup | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Yesennia Aracely has been missing since March 2022. She was last seen near Akron Stadium in Guadalajara, Jalisco, one of the host cities of the World Cup.  Jalisco is also the state with the highest number of enforced disappearances. 1  

Yesennia is one of more than 100,000 people missing in Mexico, though researchers and activists estimate the real number could be much higher. 2 Families of missing people and search groups have criticized the government for the lack of support and attention, while resources are being allocated to the World Cup.

snippet.description:
Have you ever noticed your dog constantly checking in on you? Maybe during a walk, they glance back at you as if they are making sure you’re still there? Or perhaps while you're in another room, they peek in, give you a look, and then head back to sleep.

If you notice your dog keep an eye on you, it likely indicates that your pet considers you a significant figure.
In this video, we'll explore the common reasons why dogs check in on their owners, and what it signifies for you as a caring pet owner.  Stick around to uncover what’s really behind those watchful eyes— You might be surprised at what's going on in your dog’s mind.

While they may not roam vast outdoor territories like their wild ancestors, understanding the biology of a happy dog reveals that they express ultimate contentment through very specific physiological and behavioral markers. In this video, we dive into canine evolutionary psychology to decode the 10 undeniable signs that your indoor dog is living their absolute best life.

Here’s what you’ll discover:
✅ The hidden biological markers and subtle body language that define a truly happy dog.
✅ How a well-regulated nervous system allows your indoor pet to safely drop their primal defensive barriers and engage in deep restorative sleep.
✅ The evolutionary science behind play, environmental enrichment, and why specific daily routines trigger massive oxytocin release. 🐾

Canines evolved as active foragers and pack animals, meaning their complex brains require both physical and mental stimulation to achieve homeostasis. By examining their daily indoor habits through the lens of canine science, we realize that a happy dog isn't just one that receives endless treats; it is an animal whose psychological needs for safety, mental enrichment, and pack bonding are completely met. Behaviors like exposing their vulnerable vital organs while resting, initiating play bows, and maintaining a relaxed, wiggly posture are profound physiological proofs that their indoor environment is perfectly optimized for their biological well-being.

snippet.title: New military service rules - Young Germans facing a tough decision | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
In the event of war, would you take up arms for your country? Since military service reforms came into effect in January 2026, young Germans are once again faced with this question.

That's because every 18-year-old German male is obliged to answer questions about serving in Germany’s military, the Bundeswehr, and must undergo a mandatory physical examination. The move is part of efforts to recruit more personnel.

Elias has just turned 18. A few days after celebrating his birthday, he receives a letter requiring him to complete a questionnaire for the Bundeswehr, what’s known as a "declaration of readiness". While he does think a stronger military is important, he can't imagine serving in the army himself.

Tom, on the other hand, hopes the military might offer him a career path. The 16-year-old already volunteers with the German Red Cross. At a careers fair, he explores career opportunities within the armed forces - from being a paramedic to becoming an officer.

Two other young Germans, Max and Neo, are firmly against the new military service rules. They’re helping to organize a nationwide school strike in protest - calling for greater investment in education instead.

This documentary looks at the different ways young people are reacting to the changes, from approval and aspiration to rejection and protest. Either way, it’s clear that the new military service reform is having a direct impact on a generation of Germans.

Elias has just turned 18. A few days after celebrating his birthday, he receives a letter requiring him to complete a questionnaire for the Bundeswehr, what’s known as a "declaration of readiness". While he does think a stronger military is important, he can't imagine serving in the army himself.

Tom, on the other hand, hopes the military might offer him a career path. The 16-year-old already volunteers with the German Red Cross. At a careers fair, he explores career opportunities within the armed forces - from being a paramedic to becoming an officer.

Two other young Germans, Max and Neo, are firmly against the new military service rules. They’re helping to organize a nationwide school strike in protest - calling for greater investment in education instead.

This documentary looks at the different ways young people are reacting to the changes, from approval and aspiration to rejection and protest. Either way, it’s clear that the new military service reform is having a direct impact on a generation of Germans.

Your dog is communicating with you all the time, even when they’re silent. Through tiny changes in the eyes, mouth, ears, and face, your dog is constantly giving you clues about how they feel in the moment.

Some of these signals mean calm and comfort, while others are early signs of stress or discomfort that last only a second and are easy to miss.

In this video, you’ll learn how to spot 20 subtle facial changes and understand what they really mean, so you can respond sooner, lower tension, and avoid misunderstandings before they escalate.



Whale Eye: Discomfort and need for space
Soft Eyes: Calm, trust, and emotional safety
Yawning: Stress release or social pressure
Lip Licking: Subtle discomfort or appeasement
Relaxed Open Mouth: Comfort and emotional balance
Tightly Closed Mouth: Rising tension or assessment
Mouth Corners Pulled Back: Uncertainty or mixed emotions
Ears Forward: Focus, alertness, or tension
Ears Pinned Back: Fear, appeasement, or excitement
Teeth Chattering: Stress, scent processing, or discomfort
Non-Thermoregulatory Panting: Stress or internal imbalance
Head Held High: Confidence or social pressure
Head Held Low: Insecurity or cautious exploration
Head Tilt: Processing sounds or human cues
Air Licking: Scent analysis and information gathering
Licking the Ground: Collecting detailed scent information
Sudden Drooling: Emotional overload or stress
Turning the Head Away: Polite request for space
Hard Stare: High arousal or escalation risk
Looking Away: Calming signal to reduce pressure

snippet.title: China: What do young people dream of? (2/2) | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
What do young Chinese people dream of? What hopes and goals do they have? Do the grandchildren of the "rising generation” still believe in progress through work, and prosperity for all? Or do they have different values?

In China, people rarely talk about their own dreams. There is the government’s "Chinese Dream,” of course: It promises prosperity to those who work hard and propel their country forward to the top of the world. But the boom is over, and China’s economy is stagnating. Many young people can’t find jobs. Many also no longer want to work as hard as their parents did.

In two episodes "A Day with Paintboxers, Influencers, and Millionaires” and "A Night with Rock Stars, Rebels, and Princesses,” the filmmakers meet young people who are breaking with their parents’ hopes and dreams. The subjects let the filmmakers into their homes, and open their hearts. The filmmakers, in turn, don’t talk about the young people — instead, they let them tell their own stories.

"Our generation’s dreams are completely different,” says a young woman. "My dream shouldn’t be built on my children, but on myself.” "I feel like I can try anything and achieve anything I set my mind to,” believes another. "I don’t have big ambitions,” admits a young man. "I just want to have enough money to live on so I can do what I enjoy.” And yet another emphasizes: "I don’t want to become a workhorse, but an interesting soul.”

snippet.title: How to Help a Reactive Dog Stay Calm Around Other Dogs
snippet.description:
The goal of working with leash reactivity and behavioral issues isn’t simply to stop the barking, lunging, or explosive behavior. The real goal is to help the dog overcome the fear, insecurity, and uncertainty driving those reactions in the first place.

That process often requires more than one approach. We use positive reinforcement to reward good decisions and build confidence, while also providing clear guidance and boundaries when necessary so the dog understands what is appropriate and what isn’t.

This dog came to us with severe reactivity to the point of self-harm during outbursts. Through consistent exposure, clear communication, proper timing, and the use of multiple training tools, he slowly learned how to exist calmly around other dogs.

The transformation didn’t happen because of one tool or one technique. It happened because of good coaching, owner education, and giving the dog every opportunity to succeed through a balanced approach tailored to the individual dog in front of us.

snippet.description: When was the last time you were truly alone with your own thoughts? Or completed a full task without checking social media? Or been able to sit down for a few minutes without being distracted? Our world monetizes distraction - your attention is worth more than you can imagine. But, how much does it cost you? In her talk, Yasmine will explore how technology - specifically addiction - can rewire your brain and your body, and how we can take that control back. Yasmine is a grade 8 student from Morocco and Canada who is interested in science, swimming, and reading. She is passionate about real-world issues that affect her generation. Yasmine has a deep interest in psychology & human behavior, using both personal experiences and research to understand phone addiction, attention, and the way technology shapes the modern world. She urges the audience to find their individual solution to phone addiction, bringing attention to the normalization of it. snippet.title: India's last nomads | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
This film tells the story of Ahmed and his family, camel herders in the deserts of western India. For generations, they’ve roamed the barren land with their animals, leading lives shaped by tradition and nature.

But this way of life is coming under increasing pressure: industrialization, climate change and economic challenges are rapidly transforming the region and threatening the future of nomadic life.
The film follows the family over an extended period, offering a rare insight into their daily lives. With great intimacy, it shows how they search for water sources, tend to their animals and travel through the desolate landscapes. In quiet conversations by the fire or whilst on the move, it becomes clear just how much Ahmed and his family are caught between the past and the future. They wrestle with the question of whether to continue along the old paths or to provide their children with a different, supposedly safer life.

The documentary relies on the simple power of observation. The calm, atmospheric images create an intimate connection with the protagonists, and underline what’s at stake: not just a way of life, but an understanding of how to live in harmony with nature. Relationships between people, animals and the landscape merge, in a delicate fabric - all part of a cultural heritage that may soon disappear.

The film is much more than a portrait; it exemplifies how traditional communities worldwide can be torn apart by the tensions of an accelerating present. At the same time, it invites the audience to appreciate the beauty and significance of a way of life that, despite all challenges, retains a remarkable dignity.

snippet.title: L'ultima generazione che può permettersi di sbagliare | Claudio Casisa | TEDxPoliteama
snippet.description: In un’epoca dominata dalla ricerca ossessiva della perfezione, della velocità e dall'influenza crescente dell'intelligenza artificiale, siamo costantemente spinti a confrontarci con standard irraggiungibili. Claudio Casisa, con la sua inconfondibile ironia, ci invita a fare un passo indietro, rivendicando il valore profondo e autentico delle nostre imperfezioni. Attraverso il racconto sincero e dissacrante dei suoi difetti, l’attore comico ci ricorda che il vero "supereroe" non è chi appare impeccabile, ma chi ha il coraggio di dichiararsi umano. Un invito prezioso a celebrare l'errore e il disagio come ultimi, irripetibili tratti distintivi della nostra civiltà, prima che la tecnologia ci guidi verso una perfezione priva di umanità. Claudio Casisa, comico e attore palermitano, classe '91. Nella stagione 2011-2012 partecipa insieme a “Le Malerbe” al programma televisivo Le Iene. Nel 2014 forma, insieme ad Annandrea Vitrano, il duo comico I Soldi Spicci. Il duo prende parte a diversi programmi televisivi tra cui Colorado Café e Pechino Express e realizza diverse tournée teatrali in giro per l’Italia: Femmino e maschia (2013), Chi dice donna dice camion (2019) e Tutta colpa del Poliamore (2023). Nell’autunno 2018 esce al cinema il loro primo film “La fuitina sbagliata”, distribuito da Rai Cinema e 01 Distribution. Nel settembre 2022 il duo debutta in regia con il secondo film “Un mondo Sotto Social”, prodotto da Tramp Ltd e distribuito da Medusa Film. Nel 2024 presenta il primo progetto teatrale da solista "Spaiato" e nel 2026 porta il suo nuovo monologo  di standup "Inconcludente". snippet.title: 40 Things that EMOTIONALLY Hurt Your Cat, Without You Even Realizing It
snippet.description:
Cats may appear independent and self-sufficient, but underneath their confident personality, they’re very sensitive animals who are deeply affected by our actions and how we treat them.
In this video, we’ve gathered 40 most common mistakes that even the most caring cat owners might make without realizing, mistakes that unintentionally hurt your pet’s feelings. 

#40. Picking them up incorrectly
The right way to pick up a cat is to scoop one hand under their chest, lift them up, and then hold them against your chest. Their head should be near your shoulder, and your hand should be under their bottom to support their weight. 
Picking your cat up by the scruff can cause them serious harm. While a mother cat may carry her kittens this way, your adult cat’s neck is not built to support their full weight. 
Picking a cat up by their armpits is also uncomfortable as it will put strain under his armpits from all their weight hanging down. 
Likewise, cradling a cat like a baby may look adorable, but most cats don’t like it. It makes them feel vulnerable because their tummy is exposed. Cats prefer positions where they are in control of their surroundings.

snippet.description:

His humour has had to pass more cultural crash tests than his aerospace projects.

Once a certified skydiver and tunnel flyer, today he jumps headfirst into cultural differences — using comedy to build connections where words sometimes fail.
